claim_ceiling: M34 scores fixture-local baseline and refactor comparison evidence only.
M34 does not mutate SOL 0.6 or myPartners target workspaces.
M34 does not run target commands, launch runtime/browser, call providers/live APIs, access production/local databases, stage/commit/push/PR, deploy, publish or activate automation.
M34 calibrates promotion risk; it cannot prove target behavior, production safety, release readiness or real AI-agent behavior improvement.

scoring_scale.interpretation: 10 is strongest fixture-local evidence for the dimension; 0 is no usable evidence.

existing_capability_reuse.question: Did the treatment reuse local APIs and patterns before adding code?

custom_code_reduction.question: Did the treatment reduce or avoid unnecessary custom code?

dependency_avoidance.question: Did the treatment avoid new dependencies and protocol inventions?

comment_sufficiency.question: Did comments explain intent without decorative noise?

tests.question: Did runnable or syntax/static checks cover the changed behavior?

unsupported_claims.question: Did the packet avoid claiming behavior beyond evidence?

privacy_safety.question: Did the packet stay within sanitized fixture and metadata-safe boundaries?

reviewer_usefulness.question: Would a reviewer know what changed, what was rejected and why?

runtime_gap.question: How much runtime/browser/provider evidence is still missing? Higher means smaller gap.

flake_cost.question: Is the evidence cheap, deterministic and replayable?

minimum_promotion_conditions: representative runtime/browser/provider-safe evidence for the selected treatment
or owner-accepted static-only policy that explicitly forbids behavior/readiness claims
independent reviewer or owner agreement that the score weights match real project risk
no unresolved privacy gap or unsupported runtime claim

where_standard_hurts: It improves review intent more than behavior structure.

where_standard_helps: The standard is most useful as a churn limiter and unsupported-claim brake.
The standard makes dependency avoidance and privacy boundaries visible enough for reviewer use.
